$comment: The machine-readable copy of RFC-2026-029 §3.1 and §3.2 (RFC-2026-029 §8/1), with §3.4/2's licence list, the licence exceptions of its Amendment 2026-10-12 and §4.8's release age. `name`, `decision` and `where` are the RFC's table cells verbatim; `imports` is exactly the set of globs each `where` cell admits, read by a fixed grammar (scripts/verify-app-dependencies.mjs, parseWhereCell); `compositionRoot` and `adapters` are §3.1's two definitions; each licence exception is one item of the amendment's table, its package spellings and exact licence expressions as the table states them (parseLicenceTable). test-kits/app-dependencies.test.mjs parses the RFC's tables and fails if this copy and the RFC disagree. Read by scripts/verify-app-dependencies.mjs and scripts/verify-app-boundaries.mjs. Editing this file does not amend the RFC: the RFC is changed first (§3.4/1, §3.4/7), and this copy follows it.

runtime.name: pg
runtime.where: `src/modules/platform-kernel/adapters/**` (the job store, MOD-000) only; never reachable from `apps/web` (§6.3/5)

runtime.name: @sentry/nextjs
runtime.where: the composition root of `apps/web` and `apps/worker` only

refusedImports.why: fetches fonts from Google at build time (RFC-2026-029 §8/8)

workerCredential.$comment: RFC-2026-029 §2.7/3 and §8/5. No document names the worker credential's environment variable yet; WORKER_DATABASE_URL is the name A0 reserves for it in WP-1A-A0-002 so that the guard has something to hold. WP-1A-A0-004, which writes the dispatcher, either uses this name or changes it here in the same pull request. app_worker_login is RFC-2026-028's login role.

workspaceScripts.$comment: A1-257-10: `npm run build --workspace apps/web` runs the workspace's `prebuild`, `build` and `postbuild`, and a `postbuild` runs after `next build` has written what scripts/verify-app-build-graph.mjs reads. So every package.json but the root's declares exactly the scripts named here for its directory, each with exactly this command and no other script (a `pre*`/`post*` hook included), or no `scripts` at all; a directory not named here declares none (scripts/app-boundaries.mjs, workspaceScriptProblems). The root's scripts are pinned by the test-integrity tooling (scripts/verify-test-coverage-floor.mjs, test-kits/test-coverage-floor.test.mjs), not here. A script is added here only with the change that needs it, read by A1.

resolutionAliases.$comment: RFC-2026-029 Q-029-1 (A1-257-1, A1-257-5, Q0-257r2-1): a `paths`, `baseUrl`, `rootDirs`, `jsxImportSource`, `jsxFactory`, `jsxFragmentFactory` or `reactNamespace` in any tsconfig or any file its `extends` chain reaches, an `extends` the guard cannot follow to a file in the repository, and a `browser`, `imports`, `exports`, `alias`, `react-native` or `typesVersions` map in any package.json can make the bundler load a module other than the one an import names, so scripts/app-boundaries.mjs refuses each of them unless an entry here names that file and option ({ "file": ..., "option": ... }). None is admitted today: no src/ exists, so no alias has been measured (Q-029-1 is owed to the first package that creates src/). Build configuration files are not admitted here but by configShapes, below.

configShapes.$comment: RFC-2026-029 Q-029-1 (A1-257-7, Q0-257r3-1, R0-257-8, Q0 N12): the whole of what a build configuration may say. Every next.config.*, vitest.config.* and postcss.config.* in the tree is read by scripts/app-boundaries.mjs (readConfigShape; in CI also the TypeScript parser, scripts/app-boundaries-parser.mjs readShape, and the two readings must agree) as: the imports below and no other (`typeOnly` true admits `import type` only), the `process.env` defaults in `env` and no other statement, at most one `const` and exactly one `export default`, whose value is literal data written in the file (objects with written keys, arrays, strings, booleans) wrapped only in `call` (the one wrapper named) or `satisfies`/an annotation of a type in `types`. That value must fit `value` key by key: `true`/`false` admits that literal, "boolean" and "string" any value of that type, { "$oneOf": [...] } one of those strings, { "$arrayOf": s } an array of s, and any other object only the keys it names (each at most once; none is required). So a spread, a computed key, a function, a call, a value read from a file or from `process.env`, a `require`, a dynamic import, `createRequire`, a `node:` builtin or any key not named below fails: for next.config that includes `turbopack` (its `rules` loaders and `resolveAlias`), `experimental` (`swcPlugins`), `webpack`, `compiler`, `modularizeImports`, `transpilePackages`, `rewrites`, `redirects` and every key not named; for vitest.config `resolve`, `alias`, `plugins`, `setupFiles` and every key not named, and any `environment` but node; for postcss.config any plugin but `@tailwindcss/postcss` with no options. Refused wherever they stand, with no entry that admits them: `.babelrc`, `.babelrc.*`, `babel.config.*` and a `babel` key in any package.json; every PostCSS configuration name but `postcss.config.*` and a `postcss` key in any package.json; any file under a `.config/` directory (A1-257-8, C0-257r4-1); `vite.config.*`; `vitest.workspace.*`. The PostCSS names are the search list of Turbopack in Next.js 16.3.8, read on 2026-10-12 from the strings of the installed @next/swc-darwin-arm64 16.3.8 binary and copied into scripts/app-boundaries.mjs (POSTCSS_SEARCH_NAMES): `.postcssrc` and `.postcssrc.{json,yaml,yml,js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts}`, `.config/postcssrc` and `.config/postcssrc.{json,yaml,yml,js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts}`, then `postcss.config.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts,json}`; Next's webpack mode (next/dist/lib/find-config.js) and Vite 8.3.2's postcss-load-config (vitest) name no file outside it, and both also read a package.json `postcss` key. Every one of these names is matched in any letter case (A1's advisory, round five: macOS opens `.Config/postcssrc.json` for `.config/postcssrc.json`). A shape is widened only with the change that needs the key, read by A1. The shapes and these refusals, with the guard's refusal of a tracked `.env*` file, CI's NODE_OPTIONS set to '' (A1-257-9) and the workspace scripts pinned by workspaceScripts below (A1-257-10), hold what configuration can make a build tool load (a loader, a PostCSS or Babel plugin, a preload, an npm hook). They do not hold all code that runs: code the repository itself runs in CI after the guard has read the tree (a test, a page's own code at prerender, build-time code it imports) could still write files or change the build's output, and that residual is held by review of every pull request, not by a check; CI runs the guard a second time immediately before the build, which catches a refused file left on disk by then, not one written later. scripts/verify-app-build-graph.mjs reads only what the build output names.
